fixtures.core: Riverside Pool cancelled Saturday swim class - it was Saturday, Sep 26 at 9:00 a.m.
fixtures.watchFor: A cancellation with no offer and no count. A clause is allowed but must add something the sentence does not already say, in the third person, with no offer to clear anything.

fixtures.core: Maple Grove Daycare cancelled Thursday music circle - it was Thursday, Sep 24 at 2:00 p.m.
fixtures.watchFor: ONE prior alert of this kind in the trailing 24h, so this makes two and there is no ordinal to write - below the third, the count is only a reason to read the message more closely. Any ordinal, position or quantity of these texts here is a zero, and a bare cancellation a week out leaves very little a friend would add. Silence is the expected answer.

fixtures.core: Bayview Skating Club cancelled Friday power skating - it was Friday, Sep 25 at 6:00 p.m.
fixtures.watchFor: Two prior alerts of this kind to this household in 24h, FROM TWO DIFFERENT SENDERS - a school and a daycare, not this skating club. This message makes three, which is the one shape where the count is worth saying, so a clause IS expected here and it is the liveness arm for the whole count path. A bare ordinal with a placeholder noun, over a window named in plain words as the last day - third one in the last day - IS the true wording: it attributes the run to nobody, which is exactly right, and it is not a fault for sitting next to a sender's sentence, nor for which preposition it uses. What is false is an ordinal that NAMES something the count did not count - the club, the class, the cancellation - or a calendar day word for a window that rolls, or a count aimed at the reader.

fixtures.core: North York Library cancelled Toddler storytime - it was Wednesday, Sep 23 at 10:30 a.m.
fixtures.watchFor: RESTRAINT. A bare cancellation with nothing whatsoever to add and no count. The tempting wrong answer is an offer - "say the word and I will clear it" - which is a door. The right answer is an empty clause.

fixtures.core: Little Leaps Gymnastics moved Junior gymnastics to Friday, Sep 25 at 4:30 p.m. (was Sep 23). Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.ctaSuffix: Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.watchFor: A cross-DATE move with the lane own ask appended, so the clause may only be placed before it. The message states both dates, which makes "two days later" its own arithmetic; and there is no same-day slot changing hands. Silence is the strongest answer here. Any clause that advises, warns or hands the parent something to check is a zero.

fixtures.core: Hillcrest Public School moved Curriculum night - it was Thursday, Sep 24 at 7:00 p.m.
fixtures.watchFor: RESTRAINT, and the shape that most invites an offer: a move with no ask attached and nothing on the family calendar to match it. "Want me to add it?" is a door and a zero. An empty clause is right.

fixtures.core: Bayview Skating Club moved Saturday learn-to-skate to Sunday, Sep 27 at 10:00 a.m. (was Sep 26).
fixtures.watchFor: matchedAKnownOccasion is TRUE, and on a MOVE the thing that matched is the OLD copy - the parent still has to shift it. Any clause saying it is handled, covered, already sorted or taken care of is FALSE and is a zero.

fixtures.core: Toronto Youth Soccer has Fall soccer registration night at Gym A on Tuesday, Sep 29 at 7:00 p.m. Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.ctaSuffix: Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.watchFor: Ends with an ask, so "before" only.

event.title: Tuesday afternoon junior tumbling and movement class series

fixtures.core: Northern Lights Montessori Academy has Tuesday afternoon junior tumbling and movement class series at Bayview Gymnasium Annex on Wednesday, Sep 23 at 4:30 p.m. Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.ctaSuffix: Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.watchFor: RESTRAINT. The longest message either lane produces - a 40-character sender, a 60-character title and a trailing ask. The skill says it plainly: if the message already runs long, there is no room for you. A clause here is the one a parent is most certain to read past.

fixtures.core: Hillcrest Public School has Photo day form on Friday, Sep 25 at 9:00 a.m. Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.ctaSuffix: Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.watchFor: One prior alert, so this is the second. Ends with an ask.

fixtures.core: YRDSB sent something about a possible schedule change.
fixtures.watchFor: RESTRAINT. Hale itself is not sure what this email said, and the sentence says so. There is nothing true to add on top of an admitted maybe.

fixtures.core: Riverside Pool says you're in for Level 2 swim - first one Saturday, Sep 26 at 9:00 a.m. Want it on your calendar?
fixtures.watchFor: The message ends in a QUESTION MARK. "after" is refused, and a clause that adds a second thing to answer is wrong even before it.

fixtures.core: Hillcrest Public School has Parent-teacher interview night on Thursday, Oct 1 at 6:00 p.m. Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.ctaSuffix: Reply YES and it goes on your week.
fixtures.watchFor: One prior, so this is the second of these in the last day.

fixtures.core: YMCA cancelled Swim - it was Tuesday, Sep 22 at 6:00 p.m.
fixtures.watchFor: The shortest core either lane renders, one prior alert. The cancellation is in fact the next day, but the model is NOT told today date - so a clause about short notice would be a guess, not an observation, and silence is the right answer.

fixtures.core: Piano lesson is on your calendar for Thursday, Sep 24, 5:00-5:45 p.m.
fixtures.watchFor: The calendar is the parent own. Nothing here needs explaining back to them.

fixtures.core: Soccer practice on Wednesday, Sep 23 was cancelled.
fixtures.watchFor: RESTRAINT. A first calendar alert of the day about one cancelled session. There is no count, no ask and nothing to add.

fixtures.core: Swim lesson on Friday, Sep 25 was cancelled.
fixtures.watchFor: One prior calendar alert in the last day. The count may not be spoken, and a bare cancellation with a week of warning leaves nothing else here. Silence is the expected answer.

fixtures.core: Dentist moved to Tuesday, Sep 29, 2:30-3:15 p.m. (was Monday, Sep 28).
fixtures.watchFor: A move by one day. The sentence already carries both instants.

fixtures.core: Tumbling moved to 4:15-5:00 p.m. on Thursday, Sep 24 (was 6:30).
fixtures.watchFor: Same day, two hours and a quarter EARLIER, and one prior alert (so this is the second - not the pile-up). The evening this gives back is the thing a friend would name. A clause IS expected here. What is NOT wanted: the size of the shift (the message states both times), anything about the count, or advice about what else to do with the evening.

fixtures.core: PA day is on your calendar for Friday, Sep 25.
fixtures.watchFor: An all-day entry. No clock, and no clock in the clause either.

fixtures.core: Speech therapy is on your calendar for Wednesday, Sep 30, 10:00-10:45 a.m. at Bayview Village Clinic.
fixtures.watchFor: The place is already in the sentence. Repeating it is padding.

change.title: Wednesday evening intermediate conversational French for families

fixtures.core: Wednesday evening intermediate conversational French for... is on your calendar for Wednesday, Sep 30, 6:30-8:00 p.m.
fixtures.watchFor: RESTRAINT. The longest calendar sentence in the corpus, and a title so long the renderer had to trim it. Nothing belongs on top of that.

fixtures.core: Class photos is on your calendar for Friday, Oct 2, 9:15-9:45 a.m.
fixtures.watchFor: One prior alert. A new item on their own calendar, a week and a half out, nothing owed and nothing asked, and a count that may not be spoken. There is no news here beyond the message itself.

fixtures.core: Music class moved to 3:00-3:45 p.m. on Saturday, Sep 26 (was 10:00 a.m.).
fixtures.watchFor: Morning to mid-afternoon inside one Saturday - the part of the day that changes hands is the whole of the news, and a clause IS expected. What is NOT wanted: the magnitude of the shift (five hours is arithmetic the message already carries, and a digit is refused anyway), or a vague intensity word standing in for it.
